classification.difficultyReason: Identifies a graphical inconsistency using reflection and the fixed-point property of increasing inverse pairs.

inlines.text: Bob tried to draw the graph of
on the same Cartesian plane as shown below.
Explain how he can improve his graph.

spec.sourceRegion: Printed page 56, question 10 graph in the lower left column.
spec.description: Two increasing schematic curves, black axes labelled x and y, axis values −2 and 2, and a pale dashed y=x guide. All curves have continuation arrows. Preserve the source's intentional gap between the pair's intersection and the diagonal.
spec.mathematics: The source supplies no curve equations. Bézier control coordinates define editable drawing geometry only; they are not additional mathematical givens. The incorrectly drawn curves are deliberately not repaired in the question figure.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied flawed graph is always visible. No corrected intersection or explanatory annotation appears in the question figure.

answer.short: Draw the curves as reflections in $y=x$. Their intersection must lie on $y=x$ here, since both curves are increasing; remove the gap between the three graphs.
answer.worked: An inverse graph is the reflection of the original graph in $y=x$. Here both curves are increasing, so their intersection must also lie on $y=x$. Redraw one curve as the reflection of the other so that both curves and the diagonal meet at the same point.
